name: Pre-roll
short: A ready-made joint sold at retail, typically filled with ground flower, shake or kief and sometimes infused with concentrates.
definition: A pre-roll is a factory- or hand-rolled joint sold ready to smoke. California's regulations describe it as any combination of flower, shake, leaf or kief rolled in paper, and other states use similar definitions. Infused pre-rolls add concentrates such as distillate, hash or kief to raise potency, and some states regulate them as a separate product type with different testing, labelling or tax treatment.

Pre-rolls are a popular category in many legal markets because they are convenient and give producers an outlet for smaller buds and trim. That raises recurring questions for regulators and journalists: what plant material is inside, whether the THC figure on the label reflects the actual blend, and whether infused products are tested as flower or as concentrates.

Because pre-rolls are made from flower, they are tested and tracked through the same seed-to-sale systems, and they face the same hemp-versus-marijuana issues: hemp pre-rolls made from THCA-rich flower will fall outside the federal hemp definition when total-THC rules take effect on 11 December 2026. State rule changes on pre-roll sizes, packaging and multipacks are common news items.
example: The state regulator changed its rules to let licensed retailers sell pre-rolls.

sources.name: California Code of Regulations, Title 4, Section 15000, Definitions (Department of Cannabis Control)
